def protocol.PeerSharingEngine.decodeTyp.note: the length of the message's array is read and ignored (a definite array whose length cborg's decodeListLen holds in an Int), then the key as a word; in StIdle 0 is MsgShareRequest with its Word8 amount and 2 is MsgDone, in StBusy 1 is MsgSharePeers with a definite or indefinite list of peers (decodeListWith), and any other key is refused. Agency, which the reference has in its state tokens, is the same table checked at run time; the byte limit its Cursor applies while reading is the driver's (runDecoderWithLimit, framework Driver/Limits.hs:295-331, with byteLimitsPeerSharing); a MsgSharePeers that arrives in parts is read on after the peers read whole (attemptTyped), as decodeMsg runs from the stream through mkCodecCborLazyBS (Codec.hs:42)

glue.reason: how a decoder keeps its progress on a message not all of which has arrived, so that a longer prefix is read on from where it stopped and nothing read whole is read again: the reference keeps that progress in its decoder's continuation (cborg 0.2.10.0 deserialiseIncremental, src/Codec/CBOR/Read.hs:169-172 and 1254-1260; typed-protocols 1.2.2.0 convertCborDecoderLBS, cborg/Network/TypedProtocol/Codec/CBOR.hs:136-164), fed a chunk at a time by runDecoderWithLimit (ouroboros-network framework/lib/Ouroboros/Network/Driver/Limits.hs:281-331 at c45735a5 and 4646039f); here a decoder's cursor holds it as a value. What each codec accepts and refuses, and where, is the codec's as before; each codec's incremental is its decodePrefix as the multiplexer takes it (decodePrefix is it started afresh), the reading itself in the codec's own definitions as before
